A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, Sections 1–6, Table 1, and Appendices A–C. All 25 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2 were readable, including the mathematical material.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and proof constructions, with no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes. Empirical studies mentioned are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 adds and revises mathematical results and proofs, but reports no original empirical outcomes in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: The constructive IPM, fixed-test, coverage-profile, and NLL scoring procedures remain substantively unchanged. The shift to evaluation algorithms in Section 2 changes the formal evaluability framework, assessed under T1.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The added references to pretrained models and synthetic data generation provide motivation only.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Cited density-estimation algorithms remain ingredients in theoretical arguments.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, splits, training budgets, or testing procedures. Revisions to mathematical metrics and sample-complexity bounds concern T1.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, experimental robustness tests, or empirical case studies. The revised finite-support constructions are mathematical counterexamples within proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated empirical runs, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Confidence parameters and concentration inequalities appear within theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: Theoretical result entries change: Table 1 adds non-strong-evaluability of restricted KL, and the Theorem 3.2 footnote adds a Hellinger lower bound around 1.1233. Some sample-complexity bounds are corrected. Most existing headline guarantees remain; there are no empirical performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Definition 2.3 changes quantifier order and requires guarantees for both possible model selections using one algorithm and sample bound across pairs. Definition 5.1 clips restricted KL at zero, and new Theorem 5.4 supplies a general non-strong-evaluability result with an Appendix C proof. Theorem 3.8 corrects boundedness assumptions. Appendices A–C substantially revise mathematical arguments, including a replacement coverage-profile impossibility proof, corrected concentration bounds, a revised restricted-KL counterexample, and corrected likelihood-ratio signs.

C1.justification: The broad abstract and contribution claims remain. Table 1 adds a general impossibility claim for the revised restricted-KL metric, while the introduction removes the assertion that the divergence results explain perplexity’s poor correlation with downstream tasks and narrows its restricted-KL wording.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds a conjectured extension to tail-sensitive f-divergences while explicitly excluding a blanket impossibility claim through the TV example. Section 5 clarifies restricted KL’s interpretation and explains that unrestricted positive evaluability guarantees could only be weak.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly specifies random tie-breaking for score-induced selectors. Appendix B expresses the coverage score over empirical support and explicitly defines the ratio when q(x)=0, clarifying execution of the existing rule.

R1.justification: The same cited works and principal relationships to uniform convergence, density estimation, and perplexity research are retained. Citation formatting and shortened Rényi bibliographic details do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: The six-section structure and Appendices A–C remain. v2 revises setup and proof explanations, standardizes terminology and citation wording, corrects local language, and updates acknowledgments without extensive narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: Table 1’s text and wrapping are revised within the same two-column structure. The introduction now begins on the title page, references begin on a separate page, and equation displays are reflowed. Neither version contains figures.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important foundational and proof gaps: Definition 2.3 validates either selected model, and Appendix B establishes reversed rankings where v1 only distinguished one candidate’s metric values. The nonnegative restricted-KL definition, revised counterexample, corrected likelihood-ratio reasoning, and new Theorem 5.4 materially strengthen mathematical coherence and support. These gains are substantial for a paper whose contribution is theoretical.
